news.title: Ghana vs Morocco: How Mohammed Mubarik could make Amputee World Cup history
news.lede: Ghana’s top stories, now easier to find. Discover our new search feature! Mohammed Mubarik, Ghana's leading scorer at the 2026 Amputee Football World Cup in Mexico, is on the verge of making history as the Black Challenge prepare to face Morocco in the tournament final on Sunday, November 22 (1.30 am Ghana time on Monday, November 23). The forward has scored seven goals across the competition, per WAFF, the most of any player, and stands within reach of both the Golden Boot and an unprecedented world title for his country.

news.title: UK set to host 2035 FIFA Women’s World Cup
news.lede: Everton's Hill Dickinson Stadium is one of 19 stadiums included in the 2035 bid. The United Kingdom is set to host the 2035 FIFA Women’s World Cup, with England, Northern Ireland, Scotland and Wales joining forces to stage the global football tournament. As reported by BBC Sport on Sunday, the four nations are the only bidders for the competition, with FIFA expected to formally confirm their joint hosting rights following a voting process involving national football associations at its headquarters in Zurich, Switzerland. The proposed tournament will feature 48 teams competing in 104 matches over 39 days, making it one of the biggest editions of the Women’s World Cup.

news.title: FIFA expected to approve British bid for 2035 Women’s World Cup — BBC Sport
news.lede: In Zurich, Switzerland, FIFA is expected to approve on Monday the joint bid by England, Northern Ireland, Scotland and Wales to host the 2035 Women’s World Cup. The four football associations are the only candidates to host the tournament, BBC Sport reports. A delegation from the All Together bid will be present at FIFA headquarters in Zurich. The national football associations will hold a specially arranged virtual meeting and vote to ratify the hosts of the competition.

news.title: ‘He was struggling’: Concern as World Cup winner collapses mid-interview
news.lede: Argentine World Cup winner Leandro Paredes gave reporters a fright after he collapsed mid-interview while reflecting on Boca Juniors’ latest title. Paredes was substituted off early in the second half of Boca Juniors’ 2-0 win over Atlético MG in the 2026 CONMEBOL Sudamericana final and was later put up for media duties, although the hot and humid conditions were hurting the midfielder. Leandro Paredes pictured seconds before he collapsed while in an interview, X. The 32-year-old looked tired as he entered the tunnel where media stood and managed to get through a handful of questions before suddenly he fainted.

news.title: Ghana vs Morocco: The 2 stars who could hurt Black Challenge in World Cup final

Ghana's Black Challenge will need to neutralise two of the competition's most dangerous forwards when they face Morocco in the 2026 Amputee Football World Cup final on Sunday in Mexico. According to WAFF, Ilyass Sbiyaa and Mohcine Chrharh have both registered six goals throughout the tournament, establishing themselves as Morocco's primary attacking weapons ahead of what promises to be a fiercely contested showdown.

news.title: Fifa to confirm UK as host for 2035 Women's World Cup
news.lede: Spain beat England 1-0 to win the 2023 World Cup. Fifa is set to confirm on Monday that a first football World Cup will be hosted in the United Kingdom since 1966. England, Northern Ireland, Scotland and Wales are the only bidders to jointly stage the 2035 Women's World Cup. A delegation will be present at Fifa's Zurich headquarters with national associations holding a specially arranged virtual meeting, and voting to ratify the co-hosts.

news.title: Legacy key for 2031 and 2035 Women’s World Cup says sports executive
news.lede: The 2027 Women’s World Cup takes place in Brazil from June 24 to July 25, marking the first time the tournament is held in South America. CALGARY, Canada – Focusing on the legacy of the Women’s World Cup should be the top priority for those organising the 2031 and 2035 tournaments, according to a sports executive behind the 2023 competition. In Zurich on Nov 23, FIFA will confirm that the United States, Jamaica, Costa Rica and Mexico will host in 2031, with England, Wales, Scotland and Northern Ireland on co-hosting duties in 2035. Unlike Australia and New Zealand in 2023, there will be 48 teams rather than 32, streaming giant Netflix will have some involvement and the tournaments will be held in markets more mature in terms of women’s soccer development than Australia.
